comments.author: tombert
comments.story: So Long and Thanks for All the Words: A Toast to Douglas Adams
comments.why: Funny educational standup tying anecdotes and animal facts to environment.
comments.text: I don't know what you categorize it as (I usually call it an "educational standup"), but his last talk before his death "Parrots, The Universe, and Everything" is one of the greatest things I've ever seen. It's very funny, with a lot of interesting anecdotes about his life, with a lot of interesting facts about animals, and he manages to tie the entire thing together with a pretty clever theme about the environment. I genuinely think it's one of the greatest public speeches ever done, at least in the English language. If you haven't seen it, it's an hour and a half long, and it's totally worth it: [VIDEO]

comments.author: simonebrunozzi
comments.why: Hour-long mind-blowing presentation tied to Last Chance to See.
comments.text: Douglas Adams is one of my favorite writers, and intellectuals, ever. If you are like me, you absolutely have to watch this hour-long presentation he gave at UC Santa Barbara in 2001 [0], titled "Parrots, the Universe, and Everything". Mind blowing. His last book, "Last chance to see" [1], which is about endangered species, is heavily related to that talk. I recently learned that Douglas Adams had a chance to play on stage at Pink Floyd's 28 October 1994 concert at Earls Court in London [2], playing guitar on the songs "Brain Damage" and "Eclipse". He's even responsible for the 1994 album name "Division Bell" by Pink Floyd. David Gilmour and Douglas Adams were good friends. Well, what can I say... It sucks that he went away too soon. I'd love to read more of his stuff, and I'd love to know his take on today's world. [0]: [VIDEO] [1]: [LINK] [2]: [LINK]

comments.author: dylan-m
comments.story: The Hitchhiker’s Guide to the Galaxy: 40 years of parody and predictions
comments.why: Adams's talk about Last Chance to See.
comments.text: In the same way, I'd also recommend Last Chance To See for a slightly different flavour of Douglas Adams. His whimsical style is remarkably well-suited to a non-fiction nature and travel book. I can't say I completely get his science fiction books, but I felt the constraints of a non-fiction book gave me a new appreciation for his sense of humour and his way of balancing that with thoughtful, meaningful exposition. It's one of my favourite books :) He gave a great talk about it, too: [VIDEO]

comments.author: leichtgewicht
comments.story: Hawking: AI could end human race
comments.text: [VIDEO] (Douglas Adams talking, fairly humorously, about extinction) "ending the human race" is such an interesting thing. Put aside that bone-headed nazis will tell you that humans have more than one race: We do extinct other species in incredible amounts (ask any greenpeace flyer). If we were extinguished by our own invention seems sort of fair. But by the off-chance that an AI figures out that we are actually worth being, then there might be an realistic chance that it will actually help us survive our own mistake. A bit of a gamble but if curiosity kills the cat then we are lucky to be alive anyways :)
